purpose: Comparison table of methods, libraries, and papers relevant to semantic interpretation of vector curves into garment landmarks. Read in companion with docs/research/semantic-curve-interpretation-soa-2026-05-03.md.

field_definitions.name: Display name
field_definitions.category: One of: sketch-parsing, garment-segmentation, garment-landmark, vectorization, multimodal-llm, parametric-cad, pattern-library, annotation-tool, dataset, generative-pattern
field_definitions.url: Primary reference URL (paper or project page)
field_definitions.input_type: What the method consumes; e.g. raster-stroke-sequence, vector-svg, raster-image, point-cloud, 3d-mesh, multimodal
field_definitions.output_type: What the method emits; e.g. whole-sketch-class, per-stroke-label, pixel-mask, keypoint, per-curve-label, full-pattern, vector-curves, mesh
field_definitions.granularity: whole-sketch | per-region | per-stroke | per-curve | per-keypoint | per-vertex
field_definitions.garment_aware: Whether the method has garment vocabulary out of the box; one of: yes, partial, no
field_definitions.data_requirement: What labeled data the method needs to be useful for our task
field_definitions.license: Headline license; null if unknown or not yet researched
field_definitions.role_in_v0_1: What, if any, role this plays in the v0.1 prototype
field_definitions.notes: Free-form caveats, observations, and links into related Pattern Lab docs

methods.name: Sketch-RNN
methods.data_requirement: QuickDraw-style stroke-sequenced corpus per class; not suitable for vectorized arbitrary-order beziers
methods.notes: Historical ancestor for sketch ML. Wrong granularity and wrong input format for our problem.

methods.name: Sketch-A-Net
methods.notes: Subsumed by modern multimodal classifiers (CLIP/SigLIP/DINOv2). Not a curve labeler.

methods.name: SketchGNN
methods.data_requirement: Per-stroke labeled sketches with adjacency; SPG-style. No garment taxonomy exists.
methods.notes: Right structural shape for our problem (per-stroke labels). Blocked on labeled garment-curve corpus, which the v0.1 correction loop is designed to produce.

methods.name: SketchSeg-Net
methods.notes: Requires stroke-order, which vectorized SVG does not have. Use SketchGNN-shaped models instead.

methods.name: BezierSketch
methods.notes: Belongs in the raster-to-vector preprocessing stage, before semantic interpretation begins. Quality of curve segmentation directly affects downstream labeling.

methods.name: DeepSVG
methods.notes: Useful as inspiration for tokenizing curves into model-friendly representations; not a labeler.

methods.name: Im2Vec
methods.notes: Vectorization candidate; not a labeler.

methods.name: DeepFashion2
methods.data_requirement: Photographs of clothed people; pretrained checkpoints exist
methods.notes: Closest existing keypoint vocabulary to what we need. Models are photo-trained; domain shift to line-art is a research lane. Adopt the vocabulary; defer the model.

methods.name: FashionAI Keypoints
methods.notes: Useful keypoint taxonomy reference. Photo-trained models do not transfer cleanly to vectorized line art.

methods.name: Fashion Landmark Detection (Liu et al.)
methods.notes: Earlier baseline for fashion keypoints; superseded by DeepFashion2.

methods.name: Fashionpedia / Mask R-CNN
methods.data_requirement: Fashionpedia ontology (294 garment-part classes); pretrained Mask R-CNN available
methods.notes: If the input is a photo or richly-styled render, Fashionpedia masks can act as a spatial prior fused with curve-level heuristics. Not used for clean technical flats.

methods.name: ATR (Active Template Regression)
methods.notes: Pixel-level human parsing; superseded by Fashionpedia and LIP.

methods.name: LIP (Look Into Person)
methods.notes: Pixel-level human parsing for clothed people; useful only if we accept on-body photos as input.

methods.name: OpenPose
methods.notes: Body pose constrains where garment landmarks can be on on-body croquis. Irrelevant for off-body technical flats.

methods.name: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker
methods.notes: Runs in-browser via WebAssembly; cheaper integration than OpenPose for the on-body prior.

methods.name: GarmentCode
methods.data_requirement: None for authoring; programs are hand-written
methods.notes: Parametric pattern DSL with named components and interfaces. Output side is what our SketchIntent should map into. Not a sketch parser.

methods.name: GarmentDiffusion
methods.notes: Edge-token output is a strong target shape for SketchIntent. Detailed in docs/reference/papers/RESEARCH-PAPERS-INGEST.md.

methods.name: GenPattern
methods.notes: Dual-graph (geometry+semantics) is the right separation. Pattern Lab interpretation should produce both graphs.

methods.name: SketchTailor
methods.notes: Closest existing system to the dream. Dataset/code availability unclear.

methods.name: SewFormer
methods.notes: Image-to-pattern transformer; not a per-curve labeler and not transparent enough for the v1 product surface.

methods.name: FreeSewing
methods.notes: Named landmarks (neck, hps, armhole, hem, cf) are directly reusable. FreeSewing-derived patterns are good ground truth for the heuristic interpreter to be tested against.

methods.name: Seamly2D / Valentina
methods.notes: Named-point and named-curve discipline matches the vocabulary we should adopt.

methods.name: FreeCAD Sketcher
methods.notes: Constraint-after-draw UX is the right correction interaction model.

methods.name: Onshape Sketch
methods.notes: Auto-inferred constraints with user override is the right UX shape; collaboration model is also reference for later.

methods.name: Label Studio
methods.notes: JSON-configurable schema; layout reference for the manual correction surface.

methods.name: CVAT
methods.notes: Annotation tool with team review flows.

methods.name: Roboflow
methods.notes: Predict-then-correct interaction model is the right pattern for v0.1's manual fallback.

methods.name: Labelbox
methods.notes: Enterprise annotation platform; reference only.

methods.name: COCO Annotator
methods.notes: Slot-filling UX (fixed schema, click to assign) is the right model for landmark labeling.

methods.name: GarmentCodeData
methods.notes: Renderable patterns can produce synthetic line drawings paired with known per-curve labels — the only realistic path to a labeled training corpus before user uploads accumulate.

methods.name: Deep Fashion3D
methods.notes: Provides 3D feature lines (neckline, hem, cuff). Useful as feature-line vocabulary cross-reference.

methods.name: Multimodal LLM as bootstrap labeler (GPT-4V / Claude / Gemini)
methods.notes: Useful as a bootstrap labeler to seed the corpus and as a 'second opinion' alongside the heuristic. Cost, latency, and IP/privacy are real concerns. Not the system of record.

methods.name: CLIPasso
methods.notes: Sketch generation, not labeling. CLIP has poor garment-anatomy vocabulary.

v0_1_stack: manual correction surface modeled on roboflow / coco-annotator slot-filling pattern
deepfashion2 vocabulary as cross-reference for keypoint naming
optional multimodal-llm-bootstrap as a second-opinion labeler
v0_2_additions: gradient-boosted classifier trained on the correction log
synthetic line renders from garmentcodedata as labeled corpus expansion
v0_3_additions: fashionpedia / mediapipe-pose as spatial priors when input is a photo or on-body croquis
v1_target: garmentdiffusion-shaped multimodal interpreter using genpattern dual-graph output, with the heuristic interpreter retained as a validator
